title: Prove every admissible interlocking route with an e2e test (Bun)

facts.note: Interlocking route-space artifacts and Bun e2e tests are identifiable by path.
Bun-stack realization only; other stacks own their own rendering.

values: e2e route test added, changed or removed
facts.note: Needs a diff-level observer that parses `routes:` entries and detects added/changed routes or removed covering tests.

values: bun_interlocking_coverage: declared route with no covering e2e test
facts.note: Produced by the JS detector of the bun_interlocking_coverage family.
Tester work in the e2e layer.

values: test genuinely exercises route behavior rather than only containing a token
existing proof still proves the changed route
facts.note: Whether a referencing test actually drives guard-true inputs through production resolution and execution, or still does so after a guard/trainId change, is a semantic review judgment, not observable from path or tokens.

fires: A new entry is added under `routes:` of an interlocking YAML and no e2e/**/*.ts test references its routeId or resolved trainId.
A route's guard or trainId mapping changes and its existing e2e proof is absent or no longer proves the changed route (its guard-true inputs or asserted trainId no longer match).
The detector reports a declared route with no covering e2e test.
A covering e2e test is deleted, leaving a declared route uncovered.
A route's routeId or trainId appears in e2e/**/*.ts only inside a comment: comments are masked and do not establish coverage, so the route is still uncovered.
doesNotFire: YAML under the interlocking scope that declares no `routes:` (the `_interlockings.yaml` registry index, generated projections).
A route already referenced by its routeId or resolved trainId in an e2e/**/*.ts test whose proof still exercises the route (not flagged by the detector).
A route guard/trainId change whose existing e2e proof still drives and asserts the changed route correctly.
Non-Bun stacks' e2e renderings, which are owned by their own workspace packages.

given: An interlocking YAML declares admissible routes under `routes:`
when: a declared route has no e2e/**/*.ts test exercising it
then: Write an e2e test that drives the route's guard-true inputs through production InterlockingRunner resolution, asserts the declared trainId was selected before execution, then executes that train via TrainRunner.
prefer: Read route, guard and trainId; choose guard-true inputs that distinguish it from alternative routes.
Call `new InterlockingRunner(...).resolveTrain(action, inputs)`; pass the selected train to TrainRunner and execute it.
Also assert the route- or acceptance-specific execution outcome when one is declared.
avoid: A routeId/trainId literal added only so lexical coverage sees it.
A mock resolver or hand-built substitute for production route control.
A descriptive assertion restating the plan without exercising resolution.
Bypassing TrainRunner after proving only selection.
unless: The YAML declares no `routes:` (registry index, generated projections).
The route is already referenced by routeId/trainId in an e2e/**/*.ts test: not flagged, though a token-only test still fails review.
The e2e rendering belongs to a non-Bun stack's own package.
why: Each route is a production route-control branch; unexercised, it is a silent-green gap, and a bare token passes discovery while proving nothing. Strict: an admissible route without a covering e2e test blocks.
evidence: The detector finds, for every declared route, at least one e2e/**/*.ts test referencing its routeId or resolved trainId outside comments.
Reviewer confirms the case would fail if the route guard or route-to-train mapping regressed.
Reviewer confirms the production runners (InterlockingRunner -> TrainRunner) actually execute the selected path, and that selection of the declared trainId is asserted before the train is executed.
Reviewer confirms the discoverable route/train token corresponds to behavior the case genuinely proves.
verifier_detail: JS detector (member of the bun_interlocking_coverage FAMILY) parses each interlocking artifact under plan/_trains/_interlockings/**/*.yaml and extracts declared routes (routeId/trainId/category).
Scans the consumer's e2e/**/*.ts tests for references to each route by routeId or by its resolved trainId; comments are masked so a name appearing only in a comment does not count.
A route is COVERED when at least one e2e/**/*.ts test references its routeId or resolved trainId; that token is a discovery proxy, not the testing objective.
Any declared route with no covering e2e test is flagged as a RAW violation anchored at the route's declaration line in the source interlocking YAML.
Files under the interlocking scope with no `routes:` key (`_interlockings.yaml` registry index, generated projections) carry no admissible route space and are skipped.
Per-stack discovery (here Bun e2e/**/*.ts scanned for route/train tokens) is delegated to this realization; other stacks render the same obligation in their own e2e layout.
Severity 1, disposition strict: an admissible route with no covering e2e test blocks.

Terms: admissible_route = a single entry under `routes:` of an interlocking artifact (afokapu/atdd#1248) carrying routeId, resolved trainId, category and guard_ref; the interlocking YAML is authoritative for the guarded route space and the InterlockingRunner resolves each route to exactly one trainId (afokapu/atdd#1251). silent_green_route_gap = an admissible route with no covering e2e test; its interlocking branch is never executed so CI passes while a guarded route-control path is entirely unproven.
